SMTO-SKL-0090 — SMTO can't find the Microsoft sign-in app setup

GUID: 93a813ac-4410-5630-8dad-e9fe6432e150
Slug: microsoft365-oauth-app-missing
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • To connect a Microsoft account, SMTO needs a saved entry in Parameter Store that describes your Microsoft app setup (a Microsoft OAuth App entry). No entry exists under the name that was used, so nothing was sent to Microsoft.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and look for an entry made from the Microsoft OAuth App template. If you find it, select Copy reference to copy its exact name. The connection only works when the name given matches a saved Microsoft app entry exactly.
  2. If there's none, pick Microsoft OAuth App in the template list, select New parameter, and enter the client ID, tenant and callback address from your Microsoft app registration. SMTO uses this entry to know which Microsoft app registration to sign in with.
  3. In your conversation, ask the Agent to connect your Microsoft 365 account using the copied name. Once the entry exists, it's safe to start the connection again.

What success looks like

  • The Agent gives you a Microsoft sign-in link instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the app's client secret into the conversation or the error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft profile resolution found no Parameter Store record at the exact key given as the Microsoft OAuth App reference (auth_app_ref, or an account's saved oauth_app_ref).

What this means

  • Exact OAuth app profile lookup finds no saved record. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Exact OAuth app profile lookup finds no saved record.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact auth_app_ref and intended Parameter Store profile.

How to fix it

  • Open /parameter-editor and confirm a record with profile_type microsoft_oauth_app exists at the exact key passed as auth_app_ref (or the key stored in the account's oauth_app_ref). If it is missing, create it from the Microsoft OAuth App template with the registration's client_id, tenant, client_type and exact redirect_uri, then call microsoft365.connect with that key.
  • Create a Microsoft OAuth App profile in Parameter Store with the registered client ID, tenant and exact callback URI.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The registered app's supported profile exists before connect is requested.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
